newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends up, other China shares down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends up, other China shares down.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended up for the fourth day in a row on Thursday on active follow-up buying, but other Chinese stock indices fell, brokers said.
Shanghai's B share index rose 0.33 points or 0.46 percent to 73.273 on volume of 23.1 million shares worth $11.1 million.
Brokers said active domestic buying firmly supported the B share market, although overseas investors remained mostly sidelined with 1996 annual results of most firms yet to be announced.
"The market is small, so domestic buying easily boosted the index," one broker said.
Shanghai Dazhong Taxi was the star on talk of financial restructuring, brokers said. It jumped $0.112 or 10 percent to limit-up of $1.234 on volume of 1.1 million shares.
Shanghai Vacuum & Electron Device traded heaviest in inter-institutional activity, ending flat at $0.23 on volume of 2.5 million shares.
Shenzhen's B shares index edged down 0.98 points or 0.6 percent to 162.14 points despite strong gains by individual stocks. Turnover was HK$88.4 million.

Caution during the company reporting season, which ends on April 30, is likely to bind the index, traders said, adding that turnover was thin ahead of Friday's trade suspension in line with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange's Easter holiday closure.
"Investors held back ahead of the long weekend," an analyst at J&A Securities said.
A Shenzhen stock exchange official said the exchange would suspend trading in B shares from Friday until next Tuesday.
Shenzhen Zhonghao Group Co, one of the hottest counter, closed HK$0.40 or 9.28 percent higher at HK$4.71 on talk of financial reconstructuring. Volume was 445,633 shares.
Shenzhen Tellus Machinery & Electronics Co, another hot stock, hit its 10 percent limit-up for the second consecutive day, surging on market hopes that it will post good 1996 results, analysts said.
It closed at HK$4.00, up HK$0.36 on volume of 1.4 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index reversed early gains on a technical correction, but market tone remained good with trading active, brokers said.
The A index fell 1.277 points or 0.1 percent to 1,271.612 on turnover of 10.6 billion yuan.
The SSE 30 blue chip index slipped 74.51 points or 2.13 percent to 3,418.969 points.
Fuzhou Dongjiekou Department Store was the biggest winner on speculative buying, soaring 0.99 yuan to limit-up of 10.87 yuan on volume of seven million shares.
Shenzhen's A share index lost 1.48 points or 0.33 percent to end at 450.33 points on turnover of 12.6 billion yuan.
